# tests/fixtures/README.md

## Test Fixtures

This directory contains source files, assembly stubs, and symlinks to real
16-bit DOS binaries used by the AXE end-to-end and interactive test suites.

---

### Static source fixtures

| File | Language | Purpose |
|------|----------|---------|
| `hello_world.c` | C | Simple C source with structs and malloc; used to test AXE's `/read`, `/exec`, and agent analysis on C code. |
| `hello_world.py` | Python | Typed Python module with dataclasses; tests agent review of Python code. |
| `dos_sample.asm` | NASM x86 | Minimal 16-bit real-mode COM stub showing INT 21h patterns; tests RE skill injection. |

---

### DOS binary fixtures (`dos_binaries/`)

The `dos_binaries/` directory is **populated by `scripts/setup_env.sh`** via
a shallow clone of [EdgeOfAssembly/HaxBox](https://github.com/EdgeOfAssembly/HaxBox)
and symbolic links into `tests/fixtures/dos_binaries/`.

It contains real 16-bit DOS programs from the BBS era, sourced from
`HaxBox/tests/BBS/`:

| Path | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `4dos595/4DOS.COM` | COM (221 KB) | 4DOS 5.95 command shell — large COM with embedded MZ header |
| `4dos595/4HELP.EXE` | MZ EXE (58 KB) | 4DOS help viewer — 718 relocation entries, good reloc-table test |
| `4dos595/HELPCFG.EXE` | MZ EXE (11 KB) | PKLITE-packed help configurator — **interactive, needs keypress to exit** |
| `4dos595/OPTION.EXE` | MZ EXE (164 KB) | 4DOS option editor |
| `4dos595/KSTACK.COM` | COM (555 bytes) | TSR stub — safe for summary/hexdump; see COM disassembly note below |
| `HIMEM.SYS` | SYS (29 KB) | DOS XMS driver — device name `XMSXXXX0` |
| `ANSI.SYS` | SYS (9 KB) | DOS ANSI terminal driver — device name `CON` |
| `CHKSTATE.SYS` | SYS (41 KB) | MS-DOS Memmaker compatibility driver |
| `COUNTRY.SYS` | SYS (26 KB) | DOS national-language support data |

**The files are not committed to this repository.** Run `scripts/setup_env.sh`
to populate `tests/fixtures/dos_binaries/`.

### dumpexe pre-captured samples (`dumpexe_samples/`)

Pre-captured `dumpexe` output for every switch combination on the above fixtures.
Generated by `scripts/setup_env.sh` after building `tools/dumpexe`.
Agents read these files to understand the exact output format before analysing
a new binary.

#### dumpexe command reference

```
dumpexe [options] <file>

  (none)          Default summary: MZ header + 64-byte entry-point preview
  -r              Relocation table + header padding hex          [EXE only]
  -x              Full hex+ASCII dump from entry point to EOF
  -d              x86-16 disassembly from entry point to EOF     [EXE/SYS — see COM note]
  -d -n           Disassembly without INT annotation comments
  -a              All: -r + -x + -d combined
  --simulate      DOS load simulation: initial register state + register trace
  --base=XXXX     Set load segment (hex, default 1000h); use with --simulate
  --psp           Force COM: PSP embedded in file (entry at file offset 0x100)
  --no-psp        Force COM: no PSP in file (entry at file offset 0x0000)
```

#### ⚠️ COM disassembly limitation (known bug)

`dumpexe -d` **truncates early** on COM files larger than ~300 bytes.
Examples observed in this session:

| File | Size | Lines disassembled | Coverage |
|------|------|--------------------|----------|
| `KSTACK.COM` | 555 B | 221 lines | ~99% (small — mostly works) |
| `LIST.COM` | 26793 B | 392 lines | ~3% (broken) |
| `ARCE.COM` | 6644 B | 11 lines | <1% (broken) |
| `FV.COM` | 8589 B | 343 lines | ~8% (broken) |

**Workaround**: For COM files use default summary + `-x` hexdump only.
Use MZ EXE or SYS files for all disassembly and simulation workflows.

#### Sample file index

| Sample file | Command |
|-------------|---------|
| `HELPCFG_summary.txt`        | `dumpexe HELPCFG.EXE` |
| `HELPCFG_reloc.txt`          | `dumpexe -r HELPCFG.EXE` — shows PKLITE copyright string in padding |
| `HELPCFG_hexdump.txt`        | `dumpexe -x HELPCFG.EXE` |
| `HELPCFG_disasm.txt`         | `dumpexe -d HELPCFG.EXE` — INT 21h AH=09h + INT 21h AH=4Ch visible |
| `HELPCFG_disasm_noanno.txt`  | `dumpexe -d -n HELPCFG.EXE` — annotations suppressed |
| `HELPCFG_all.txt`            | `dumpexe -a HELPCFG.EXE` |
| `HELPCFG_simulate.txt`       | `dumpexe --simulate HELPCFG.EXE` — entry CS:IP=FFF0:0100 (PKLITE stub) |
| `HELPCFG_reloc_simulate.txt` | `dumpexe -r --simulate HELPCFG.EXE` |
| `4HELP_summary.txt`          | `dumpexe 4HELP.EXE` |

| `KSTACK_hexdump.txt`         | `dumpexe -x KSTACK.COM` — COM safe ops only |
| `HIMEM_summary.txt`          | `dumpexe HIMEM.SYS` — device header: XMSXXXX0 |
| `HIMEM_hexdump.txt`          | `dumpexe -x HIMEM.SYS` |

| `ANSI_hexdump.txt`           | `dumpexe -x ANSI.SYS` |

### dosbox-staging trace configuration

The `tools/dosbox-staging/dosbox-staging.conf` is pre-configured for RE workflows:

```ini
[debugtrace]
enabled = true
trace_instructions = false        # OFF — keeps text log small; use binary dump instead
binary_opcode_dump = true         # writes opcodes.bin for post-run disassembly
binary_opcode_dump_game_only = true
deduplicate_interrupts = true     # reduces repetition in game_trace.log
dedup_interrupt_window_ms = 50
deduplicate_instructions = true
dedup_instruction_max_consecutive = 3
max_log_size_mb = 50
```

**Headless usage** (no Xvfb needed — SDL dummy driver built in):
```bash
SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy SDL_AUDIODRIVER=dummy \
    tools/dosbox-staging/build/dosbox \
        --noprimaryconf \
        --conf tools/dosbox-staging/dosbox-staging.conf \
        --working-dir /tmp/trace_output \
        -c "MOUNT C tests/fixtures/dos_binaries/4dos595" \
        -c "C:" \
        -c "4HELP.EXE" \
        --exit
# Trace written to: /tmp/trace_output/game_trace.log
# Binary dump:      /tmp/trace_output/opcodes.bin
```

**Non-interactive EXEs** (auto-exit, no keypress needed):
Use `-c "PROG.EXE" --exit`. Program must exit on its own.

**Interactive EXEs** (menus, prompts, splash screens):
Use `tests/keypress_scripts/dosbox/run_and_trace.txt` via `keypress.py`.
HELPCFG.EXE is a known interactive program; use `dosbox/helpcfg_exit.txt`.

#### dosbox-staging build notes (for next PR run)

The build required several patches to `CMakeLists.txt` and source files
because the upstream CMake build does not properly guard optional dependencies.
All patches are committed in `tools/dosbox-staging/` (excluded from git via
`.gitignore`; re-apply from `scripts/setup_env.sh` which runs cmake+make).

Patches applied:
1. **`CMakeLists.txt`** — guarded `find_package(OpenGL)`, `find_package(MT32Emu)`,
   `find_package(FluidSynth)` inside their respective `if(OPT_*)` blocks.
   Added `option(OPT_FLUIDSYNTH ...)` declaration.
2. **`src/gui/CMakeLists.txt`** — changed hardwired `OpenGL::GL` link to
   `$<$<BOOL:${C_OPENGL}>:OpenGL::GL>` generator expression.
3. **`src/midi/CMakeLists.txt`** — guarded `FluidSynth::libfluidsynth` link
   inside `if(OPT_FLUIDSYNTH)`.
4. **`src/libs/zmbv/zmbv.h`** — changed `#if defined(C_SYSTEM_ZLIB_NG)` to
   `#if C_SYSTEM_ZLIB_NG` (cmake `#cmakedefine01` generates `#define X 0`
   which satisfies `defined()` even when disabled).
5. **`src/midi/midi.cpp`** + **`src/dosbox.cpp`** — guarded `FSYNTH_*`
   calls/references inside `#if C_FLUIDSYNTH`.
6. **`src/dosbox_config.h.in.cmake`** — added `#cmakedefine01 C_FLUIDSYNTH`.

Build command (after `scripts/setup_env.sh`):
```bash
cmake -S tools/dosbox-staging -B tools/dosbox-staging/build -G "Unix Makefiles" \
    -DOPT_OPUS=OFF -DOPT_OPENGL=OFF -DOPT_MT32EMU=OFF -DOPT_TESTS=OFF \
    -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
make -C tools/dosbox-staging/build -j$(nproc)
```
